3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-21, density v4 — 'pack the houses tighter, and shrink the bare brown ground disc'): the house cluster's share of the BUILT GROUND's radius, so a settlement's footprint is r_house / this and the ring from the last house out to the footprint's edge is built ground with no houses on it (定居点周边和地图上的地形要有一定距离的缓冲过渡). It replaces house_radius_ratio, which pointed the other way: the footprint came from population and the houses took a share of it, so shrinking the disc only forced that share up and cancelled the shrink (density v2). The cluster is the primitive now; the disc is derived from it. 0.53 is not a free look choice. The footprint mask fades from 1 at 0.3 of its radius to 0 at its edge, and a house candidate needs foot >= house_foot_min (0.55), which lands at 0.53 of the radius on average — so a cluster wider than that simply has its outer ring refused, which is the whole of the difference measured over the real pack at IDENTICAL cluster radii: 0.53 gives 87-93% of every group's target placed and 24 of 684 settlements reduced to their landmark alone, while the 0.78 first proposed gives 78-82% and 36. Raising it means lowering house_foot_min in step, or the cluster is truncated and the outer ring quotas are spent inward

3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-21, density v5 — '每一个等级的定居点房屋数量要差不多，并且忽略房屋和地图的真实比例的大小，尽量贴近AI原图模型的生成游戏模型'; the counts he then fixed himself, '从大到小：100/80/50/30/20'). The five groups' counts were 100/60/24/20/9 — a village a tenth of a capital — and a settlement's TIER is meant to read from what stands in it (palace / church tower / church / chapel, townhouses against thatch), not from how many roofs it has. The range is compressed to under 5:1 and every house is 2x its real-world size (data/map3d_houses.csv, tools/map3d/scale_houses.py): the world is built at 50 m per pack px, so a true-to-life cottage was 7-12 px at the closest zoom and a settlement read as gravel scattered on bare ground. Because a house now covers 2x the GROUND it did, the per-group m2 rows had to move with the counts or the same count would simply spread over twice the area — they are set just over the packing floor instead, which is what makes the weave tighter rather than merely bigger. This row is the capital's ground per house in square metres (was 400, at half the house area): the tightest weave of the five. Cut from the v5 first pass (760/800/880/900/1000) in the same round, because the packer stopped reserving a SQUARE of each building's long side and started reserving its real rectangle (bake_houses.half_extents), which handed back the ~37%% of every plot that a 14 x 10 m cottage's 14 x 14 m square was holding as air. The value is each group's measured PACKING FLOOR — swept on bake_houses' own flat, fully buildable canvas (tools/map3d/test_bake_houses.py's fixture), the smallest ground per house at which the group still seats its FULL target: capital 740, city 740, town 700, fort 700, village 700 (the worst of six seeds on that canvas, not one lucky layout). Re-measured 2026-09-22, when the owner pulled every house to about one size (房屋大小近似): the 12 m cottage grew to 16 and the 32 m longhouse shrank to 20, and since the cottages are the commonest types by weight the MEAN plot grew, so the old floors (660/660/700/640/640) started costing a capital 4 houses, and one step tighter costs 14-22%% of the count because the ring quotas start pushing houses outward instead of packing them. It is therefore as tight as this layout packs, not a look preference.

3D bake houses: the largest ground gradient (rise over run) a house may stand on — the pack's own 93rd-percentile land slope (assets/3D/terrain/<map>/bake/world.json's slope_percentiles[1]), where bake_world.py's t_rock (ramping from the 82nd percentile) reaches FULL strength, so the rule is a house stands anywhere the ground is not fully drawn as rock; a new pack should read its own world.json rather than assume 0.62

3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-24: 要垂直于地面，不可以被地面遮住部分): the most the ground may fall across a house's own rotated footprint (bake_houses._footprint_drop, a 3 x 3 grid) — the runtime stands every house on its HIGHEST ground over a stone foundation down to its lowest, so this is the tallest foundation a house may need; a steeper plot is refused and the house placed elsewhere (measured on beria: 7.7% of plots)

3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-24): the same for a settlement's landmark, whose footprint is 2-4x a house's — its spot search takes the NEAREST spot within this fall, else the flattest it found (a church across a 155 m fall stood on a tower of stone)
3D bake houses: a house stays this many metres from water

3D bake houses (2026-09-21): how far a house's own EDGE stays clear of a river's drawn water edge — bake_houses adds the building's own half-size to it, so this is the gap itself and not a centre-to-water distance. It covers the runtime's bank wobble (map3d_river_bank_wobble_amp 0.3 of the local width) at the sizes most courses run. `land` is the COASTLINE's mask and never knew about rivers, which is how a riverside town came to stand in the water, with barns adrift on the blue. It is deliberately NOT the sea's house_shore_min_m (25 m) and is NOT folded into the land gate: _dry() would then hold every house 25 m back from its own river, and Shole, a town of 50, came out with four buildings and a bridge to an empty bank. A medieval town stands ON its river.
3D bake houses: a burg with is_port 1 may build this close to the water instead

Never the sea, never a river's channel or banks

3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-25: 标志性建筑要在中间附近 — the houses round the palace all faced one way, packed to one side of it): a settlement is laid out round its LANDMARK's own spot, with an open square this many metres wide on every side of the landmark's walls, and a lane round the square whose frontage houses face the landmark

3D bake houses: how far bake_houses.place() searches outward, in rings, for land clear of the shore buffer when the burg's own centre fails it — a port's registered point can sit right on the water; the landmark is placed there instead, offset from (0,0). This is an outer bound only: the search is also capped by house_radius_ratio x the settlement's own footprint radius, so a relocated landmark never lands past its own cluster in the buffer ring meant to stay empty. Nothing found leaves the settlement with no landmark and no houses at all

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2 (spec 2026-09-20): a flat count budget spent by a single greedy nearest-first fill cuts a hard circle — full density, then nothing, however far short of r_house that budget runs out (measured: a capital's fill stopped at 220 m of its own 342 m). The group's target is instead split into this many concentric ring quotas (richest at the centre, thinning by house_edge_falloff_gamma), so the outermost ring still gets a nonzero share and the cluster is built to reach near r_house rather than exhaust itself in one dense core. If real terrain leaves a ring short of its own quota (a shore, a slope, a small island), bake_houses.place() spends the shortfall on whatever ring still has room rather than leaving it unbuilt, so the group's target is still reached wherever the settlement's own ground allows it

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2: how hard the ring quotas thin from centre to rim — weight(ring) = (1 - ring's own mid-radius fraction) ^ this, so 1.0 is a straight linear taper and higher values spend more of the budget on the core, leaving the rim sparser still (a NEW gamma, unrelated to the removed house_density_gamma: that one scattered points with no lanes at all and was rejected outright; this one only grades how a FIXED total spends its ring quotas across a network that already has its own negative space from the lanes)

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2: the horizontal scale (independent of the 0.92..1.08 per-house jitter) a house at r_house itself shrinks to, tapering from 1.0 at the centre — paired with house_height_min so the rim reads smaller AND lower, not just sparser

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 1: lane frontage was supplying essentially the whole per-group target before block fill ever got a slot (measured: 399 of a capital's 400), so the town read as a starburst of strings with empty wedges between the lanes. Caps what the frontage pass may take of EACH ring's own quota to this share, reserving the rest for block fill — most of a medieval town's buildings sit behind the street frontage, not on it. Applied within the ring-quota system (a share of quotas[ring], not of the flat total) so the edge feathering is unaffected; if capping frontage leaves a ring's remainder unfillable by infill (small blocks, refusing terrain), the leftover pass lets frontage take it back rather than lose it

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a small or narrow site (a harbour village whose buildable land is a sliver, most of its r_house being open water) can leave a settlement at just its landmark plus one house — not from lack of room, but because the plot_step_m infill grid never happens to land a candidate in the sliver that IS buildable (measured on one such village: 4 of 96 candidates passed at the normal 10 m step, 49 of ~1500 at a third of it). Only spent as a last-resort top up once every other pass has left the settlement short of its target, so it changes nothing for a settlement that already reaches its target

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a second, separate cause found on a real settlement (chawbigdon, a city) -- not water, not slope (both clear everywhere in its disc), but the footprint/built-ground mask itself sat at ~0.48 at the settlement's OWN centre and fell further outward, on land otherwise flat and dry (bake_world.py's own footprint_edge_noise fraying low across this one disc, out of this module's reach). The absolute last resort: house_foot_min scaled by this ratio, tried only once the fine grid above has ALSO failed. Never touches the shore or slope tests, so a genuinely steep or wet site (verified separately: apton, aringham -- 100% slope failures well past the threshold) is still correctly left at its landmark
